en.name: iPlantPulse
en.subtitle: Remote for your own hub
en.short_description: TV remote, light control and a gamepad for a smart-home hub you run yourself.
en.description:
iPlantPulse is a control surface for a smart-home hub you run yourself. Point it at your hub's address and it becomes a remote for whatever that hub drives.

FOUR CONTROLLERS
• TV — a full remote with a D-pad, transport keys, a number pad, and channel and volume rockers.
• Lights — per-room brightness, colour temperature, and a colour wheel, with an all-off button.
• Gamepad — dual analog sticks, a D-pad, and face and shoulder buttons.
• Hub — your devices in one list, a live reachability check of your hub, and a log of the commands you have sent this session.

YOUR HUB, YOUR RULES
iPlantPulse talks to an HTTP endpoint you give it. There is no iPlantPulse cloud and no account, and commands go straight from your phone to your hub with no third-party service in between. Apart from your hub, the app sends a crash report if it crashes, and it shows ads from Google AdMob. Google may use device identifiers to serve and measure those ads. The app never asks for permission to track you (there is no App Tracking Transparency prompt), and where the law requires consent (the EEA, the UK and Switzerland) ads load only after you have made a choice in Google's consent form, which you can change later under Settings > Privacy choices. If you do not enter a hub address the app runs against a built-in simulator so you can try every control before you wire anything up — and it tells you plainly that it is simulating.

BUILT TO FEEL RIGHT
Haptics on every press, live command feedback, and a transport status indicator so you always know whether a button actually reached the hub. If the hub rejects a TV or light command, that control goes back to the last setting the hub accepted instead of showing a change that never happened.

Available in English, Arabic, Chinese (Simplified), French, German, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian and Spanish.
en._name_note: iPlantPulse, not PlantPulse: another developer holds 'PlantPulse' on the App Store and Apple answers 409 'The app name you entered is already being used'. That 409 failed the whole deliver run, not just the name, so the screenshots never uploaded either.

review_information.notes:
2. DEVICES AND OS VERSIONS TESTED
Automated tests run on every build: iPhone 17 Pro Max and iPad Pro 13-inch simulators on iOS 26, and a Pixel Android emulator on API 34.
Each release is also installed and launched on those targets, so a
build that cannot start never ships.

3. WHAT THIS APP DOES, AND FOR WHOM
iPlantPulse is a control surface for a smart-home hub you run yourself. Point it at your hub's address and it becomes a remote for whatever that hub drives.

Intended audience:
Remote for your own hub

4. SETTING UP AND REACHING THE MAIN FEATURES
No account and no login are required. Every feature is reachable from the first screen after launch.
Without a hub address the app drives a built-in simulator and says so in a banner on every controller screen, so every control can be tried without hardware. To send real commands, enter a hub address in Settings (the chip at the top right of any controller screen); the app then POSTs each command to <address>/remote/command and checks <address>/health.
iOS asks for Local Network access the first time the app contacts a hub address; nothing on the network is contacted before the user saves one.

5. EXTERNAL SERVICES USED
- The hub address the user enters in Settings (HTTP or HTTPS, usually a device on the user's own network). The app has no backend of its own.
- Firebase Crashlytics (Google): a crash report (stack trace, device model, OS version) when the app crashes or hits an unhandled error. Not linked to a user and not used for tracking. Firebase Analytics and Performance Monitoring are linked through a shared library but are deactivated in Info.plist / AndroidManifest.xml and never started.
- Google AdMob (ads): banner and occasional interstitial ads served by Google. Google may use device identifiers to serve and measure ads; the app does not track users across other companies' apps or websites. Where required (EEA, UK, Switzerland) consent is requested before any ad, and the choice can be changed under Privacy choices in the app.

6. REGIONAL DIFFERENCES
The app ships 12 languages (Arabic, Chinese (Simplified), English, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish). Features are identical in every region.

7. REGULATED INDUSTRY OR THIRD-PARTY MATERIAL

The app is not in a regulated industry and carries no licensed third-party material. All content, artwork and copy are the developer's own.


ACCOUNT DELETION
The app creates no account, so there is nothing to delete.
